## Description

This PR adds the ability for the `OllamaLLMClient` to auto-discover model features (`capabilities` in Ollama's terminology) using the `show` API. This eliminates the need to manually maintain a mapping from model families to known feature sets. If the auto-discovered features don't return `True`, it falls back to the existing logic for backwards compatibility.

author: perigrin
body:
## Summary

Implements the critical missing `FindCompatibleVersion` method and related recovery functionality to resolve GitHub Issue #312. This prevents users from being stranded with broken PVM installations after failed updates by providing automatic compatible version detection and recovery.

## ✨ Key Features

### 🔍 Compatible Version Detection
- **`FindCompatibleVersion()`** method with comprehensive platform compatibility checking
- GitHub API integration to query available releases including prereleases  
- Intelligent version selection preferring stable over prerelease versions
- Cross-platform compatibility validation for Linux, macOS, and Windows

### 🛠️ Enhanced Recovery System
- **`downloadCompatibleVersion()`** method for automatic recovery downloads
- Integration with existing validation and verification infrastructure
- Atomic binary replacement with proper permission handling
- Comprehensive error handling with detailed error messages

### 🖥️ Platform Support
- **Linux**: AMD64, ARM64 architectures
- **macOS**: Intel (AMD64), Apple Silicon (ARM64) 
- **Windows**: AMD64 architecture
- Automatic platform detection and asset filtering

## 🧪 Testing

### Comprehensive Test Coverage
- ✅ **Unit tests** covering all recovery scenarios and edge cases
- ✅ **Integration tests** for end-to-end recovery workflows  
- ✅ **Benchmark tests** for performance validation
- ✅ **Error injection testing** for robust failure handling

### Test Results
- **All existing tests pass** - no regressions introduced
- **Cross-platform compatibility** verified through asset filtering tests
- **Network resilience** with graceful GitHub API rate limiting handling

## 🏗️ Architecture

### Recovery Strategy Integration
The implementation integrates seamlessly with the existing recovery system:
- `ScenarioIncompatibleBinary` triggers compatible version search
- Fallback to manual rollback if compatible version unavailable
- Non-automatic recovery requiring user confirmation for safety

### Security & Reliability
- 🔒 HTTPS-only downloads with checksum validation
- 🛡️ Binary format verification (ELF, Mach-O, PE)
- ✅ Platform compatibility checks before download
- ⚛️ Atomic file operations to prevent corruption

## 🚀 Performance Optimizations

- Efficient GitHub API usage with proper error handling
- Standard library string matching (replaced custom implementation)
- Pre-allocated slices where performance matters
- Graceful handling of rate limiting and network failures

## 🔧 Implementation Details

### Key Methods Added
```go
func (rm *RecoveryManager) FindCompatibleVersion() (*version.UpdateInfo, error)
func (rm *RecoveryManager) downloadCompatibleVersion(ctx *RecoveryContext) error
```

### Enhanced Features
- Platform-specific failure detection and diagnosis
- Improved error messages with context
- Documentation for magic numbers and design decisions

## 🧪 Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests for `FindCompatibleVersion` method
- [x] Integration tests for complete recovery workflows
- [x] Error handling tests for network failures
- [x] Platform compatibility validation tests
- [x] Performance benchmark tests
- [x] Cross-platform asset filtering tests

## 📊 Impact

### Before
- ❌ Failed updates could leave users with broken PVM installations
- ❌ No automatic recovery from incompatible binary scenarios
- ❌ Manual intervention required for all recovery scenarios

### After  
- ✅ Automatic detection and download of compatible versions
- ✅ Robust recovery from incompatible binary failures
- ✅ Comprehensive error diagnosis and recovery strategies
- ✅ Cross-platform support with proper validation

## 🔗 Related Issues

- Closes #312: Implement updater recovery with compatible version detection
- Addresses critical reliability gap in PVM update system
- Prevents users from being stranded with broken installations

## 🚀 Future Enhancements

Potential future improvements identified during implementation:
- Caching layer for GitHub API responses to improve performance
- Circuit breaker pattern for enhanced reliability  
- Additional binary signature verification for security
- Metrics and telemetry for recovery success rates

author: austinmatherne-wk
body:
#### Reason for change
The function that determines whether plugins passed to the Session API require loading CLI options (and applying their default values to RuntimeOptions) did not account for plugin dependencies.

As a result, the following would throw an attribute exception because `options.configFile` wasn't set by EDGAR/render.
```python
options = RuntimeOptions(
    entrypointFile="/Users/austinmatherne/Documents/xbrl/filings/workiva/0001445305-25-000091-xbrl.zip",
    disclosureSystemName='efm-pragmatic',
    logFile="/Users/austinmatherne/Desktop/arelle.log",
    plugins='EDGAR',
    validate=True,
)
with Session() as session:
    session.run(options)
```

Whereas this would not (note the addition of `EDGAR/render` which is already a dependency of `EDGAR`):
```python
options = RuntimeOptions(
    entrypointFile="/Users/austinmatherne/Documents/xbrl/filings/workiva/0001445305-25-000091-xbrl.zip",
    disclosureSystemName='efm-pragmatic',
    logFile="/Users/austinmatherne/Desktop/arelle.log",
    plugins='EDGAR|EDGAR/render',
    validate=True,
)
with Session() as session:
    session.run(options)
```

#### Description of change
For the Session API, also check whether plugins imported by user-specified plugins define CLI arguments that need to be loaded.

* CI

@Arelle/arelle

- disconnect WiFi

- Connect to network

the network pane

Successfully logged into ArgoCD server

Error executing sync command: Command failed: argocd app sync 'go-rmeqhzrj-development' --insecure

author: jez
body:
<!-- (optional) Explain your change, focusing on the details of the solution. This is a great place to call out user-visible changes. -->


### Motivation
<!-- Why make this change? Describe the problem, not the solution. This can also be a link to an issue. -->

This adds 8 bytes to every `ClassOrModule` symbol to store the package that
owns this `ClassOrModule`.

Unfortunately, this memory increase affects all Sorbet users, not just those
runs that use `--stripe-packages`. That being said, we think that the effective
increase in memory usage here will be relatively small. Stripe's codebase only
has something like 2 million `ClassOrModule` definitions, so this only
translates to something like 16 MB.

This PR technically adds two fields. The `packageRegistryOwner` is an
implementation detail that makes it easier to compute `package` with as little
processing as possible. If we did not compute and store `packageRegistryOwner`
for every class, it would be a little more work to walk the package hierarchy
in `enterClassSymbol`. If we just added the `package` field to `ClassOrModule`,
the size would increase by 8 bytes anyways, because the class must be 8-byte
aligned. So I figured I'd use those 4 would-be padding bytes as an optimization
for computing `package`.

After this change, the only uses of `getPackageNameForFile` are those that
operate on files--there are no more calls where we're calling `sym.loc().file()`
to get the package for a symbol.


### Test plan

author: rmaynardap
body:
It is possible for a definition to reach needs_apply based on configured options, when a valid plan file does not exist. Currently it will still attempt to execute terraform, which will fail with an error code when there is no plan file and halt the execution of the rest of the deployment. This changes the behavior by checking if a plan file exists. 

Secondarily, plan files were retained after they were applied (unless using S3 remote storage for plan files in conjunction with a run-id). This causes future runs to not plan, the internal deploy tooling we use covered this up because it removes plan files prior to running a plan, but a consumed plan will never be valid as the lineage will change, so there is no value in keeping a previously applied plan file. This does not affect or change behavior of the console output log for prior plans.

body:
## Summary
- Introduces a full-featured NeRF Edge Kit supporting real-time neural radiance fields for spatial computing.
- Adds iOS native modules with Metal and ARKit integration for high-performance rendering and eye tracking.
- Implements Python core modules for model configuration, scene management, training, optimization, and deployment.
- Provides advanced rendering techniques including foveated rendering and neural engine acceleration.
- Supports multi-platform deployment with export utilities for Core ML, ONNX, TensorRT, OpenVINO, TensorFlow Lite, and WebGPU.

## Changes

### iOS Native Modules
- **ARKitIntegration.swift**: AR session management, eye tracking simulation, scene capture, and coordinate conversions.
- **FoveatedRenderer.swift**: Metal-based foveated rendering pipeline with quality levels and gaze-driven rendering.
- **MetalNerfRenderer.swift**: Metal compute and render pipeline for NeRF inference and rendering.
- **NeuralEngineAccelerator.swift**: Neural Engine and Metal Performance Shaders acceleration for optimized model inference.
- **NerfEdgeKit.swift**: Singleton interface combining Metal renderer, ARKit integration, neural accelerator, and foveated renderer.
- **NerfModel.swift**: NeRF model loading, inference with CoreML or Metal, and positional encoding.
- **MetalShaders.metal**: Metal shader code for vertex, fragment, compute kernels including foveated rendering.
- **Info.plist**: iOS app permissions and capabilities for camera and ARKit.

### Python Core Modules
- **__init__.py**: Package initialization with versioning and device info utilities.
- **core/config.py**: Data classes for model, training, scene, and optimization configurations with presets.
- **core/scene.py**: Scene representation, camera models, COLMAP and transforms.json loading, ray generation, and dataset.
- **models/nerf.py**: Standard NeRF model with positional encoding, MLPs, hierarchical sampling, and volume rendering.
- **models/instant_ngp.py**: Instant Neural Graphics Primitives implementation with hash encoding and spherical harmonics.
- **optimization/quantization.py**: Model quantization, pruning, knowledge distillation, and benchmarking utilities.
- **training/trainer.py**: Comprehensive training pipeline with multi-GPU support, mixed precision, logging, and checkpointing.
- **deployment/export.py**: Cross-platform model export utilities for Core ML, ONNX, TensorRT, OpenVINO, TensorFlow Lite, and WebGPU.

## Test plan
- Validate iOS app builds and runs on iOS 17 devices with ARKit support.
- Run Python training scripts with sample datasets and verify model convergence.
- Export models to various deployment formats and test loading on target platforms.
- Benchmark rendering performance and neural engine acceleration on supported devices.
- Verify foveated rendering quality adapts to simulated eye tracking data.
- Confirm scene loading from COLMAP and transforms.json formats works correctly.
- Perform quantization and pruning on models and validate accuracy retention.
- Test training with mixed precision and distributed setups.

This PR establishes a robust foundation for real-time NeRF applications across mobile, desktop, and web platforms with advanced optimization and deployment capabilities.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This change introduces a new feature to improve performance by lazy-loading the Mermaid.js diagramming library.

The implementation consists of several new, reusable utilities:
- A generic `Observer` class for pub/sub patterns.
- A `first-interaction` detector that fires an event on the first user activity (click, scroll, etc.).
- A `dom` utility with a promisified `addScriptToHead` function for loading external scripts.

This system is used to implement the Mermaid lazy-loading. On first user interaction, the code now:
1. Finds all code blocks intended for Mermaid rendering (i.e., with the class `language-mermaid`).
2. Adds the `mermaid` class to them to prepare them for rendering.
3. Injects the Mermaid.js script from a CDN into the page head.

This prevents the Mermaid.js library from being downloaded and parsed during the initial page load unless it's actually needed, which is determined by the user's interaction with the page.

body: Add `.js` extensions to server-side relative imports to fix module resolution errors and enable backend startup. The backend server failed to start with "Cannot find module" errors after compilation due to Node.js ESM's strict requirement for explicit file extensions in relative imports. This PR implements a comprehensive paywall and monetization system for QuickNote Pro, enabling users to purchase premium themes and features through both monthly subscription ($2.99) and lifetime purchase ($14.99) options.

## Key Features

### Pro Theme System
- **3 Premium Themes**: Futuristic (cyberpunk-inspired), Neon (vibrant creative), and Floral (nature-inspired)
- **Visual Theme Picker**: Interactive grid with live previews and Pro theme gating
- **Seamless Integration**: Accessible from Settings → Theme & Appearance with instant application

### Paywall Experience
- **Context-Aware Messaging**: Different entry points (theme picker, settings) provide tailored upgrade flows
- **Clear Value Proposition**: Prominent "One-time purchase, no subscription" messaging for lifetime option
- **Purchase Restoration**: Reliable restore functionality for existing customers
- **Error Handling**: Graceful fallbacks when entitlement checks fail

### Analytics & Business Intelligence
Comprehensive event tracking for optimization:
- `paywall_shown` - Track display frequency and entry points
- `paywall_conversion` - Monitor purchase success rates
- `upsell_entry_point` - Identify most effective upgrade triggers
- `failed_payment` - Debug payment issues and user friction

### User Experience Flow
1. User selects Pro theme → Paywall displays with theme context
2. Clear pricing comparison with savings highlight (75% off for lifetime)
3. Purchase completion → Instant theme unlock and application
4. Pro status persists with visual indicators throughout app

## Technical Implementation

### Services Architecture
- **ThemeEntitlementService**: Manages Pro access, purchase state, and subscription validation
- **PaywallAnalyticsService**: Tracks business metrics with structured event logging
- **Enhanced ThemeService**: Dynamic theme loading with Pro theme support

### Quality Assurance
- **Comprehensive Test Coverage**: Unit tests for entitlement logic, purchase flows, and analytics
- **Developer Tools**: Debug-only testing utilities for rapid development iteration
- **Error Resilience**: Graceful degradation when services are unavailable

### Accessibility & Localization
- **Global Ready**: Structured for multi-language and regional pricing support
- **Screen Reader Compatible**: Proper semantic markup and focus management
- **High Contrast Support**: Pro themes maintain accessibility standards

## Demo Usage

```dart
// Check theme access
if (entitlementService.shouldShowPaywallForTheme('futuristic')) {
  // Show paywall with context

    entryPoint: 'theme_picker',

    specificFeature: 'futuristic',
  );
}

await themeService.setSelectedTheme('futuristic');
```

The switch from using `ssid` in the backend to `ssuId` keeps things consistent with other queries where STOCKING_STANDARD_UNIT_ID is actually `ssuId`. 


In the accordion title of a standard unit, the ssid is using the s_r_id value because users have been using that term since when affordability was great and most people didn't have a second job, so a long time ago.

author: matthewdale
body:
[GODRIVER-3638](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/GODRIVER-3638)

## Summary

* If `SetFailPoint` is called when `mtest` is connected to a sharded topology.
* Add an `mtest` option `AllowFailPointsOnSharded` to allow using failpoints on sharded topologies.

## Background & Motivation

On sharded topologies, failpoints are applied to only a single mongoS. If the driver is connected to multiple mongoS instances, there's a possibility a different mongoS will be selected for a subsequent command. In that case, the failpoint is effectively ignored, leading to a test failure that is extremely difficult to diagnose.

Note that if we implement [GODRIVER-3328](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/GODRIVER-3328), we no longer need to prohibit using failpoints on sharded topologies.

    *   The search results provide comprehensive statistics for each doctor, such as total prescriptions, the number of unique medications prescribed, active days, and the dates of their first and last prescriptions.

*   **Centralized Reports Page:**
    *   Introduced a new main reports page (`/reports`) that serves as a central hub, providing easy access to both the new Doctor Search and the existing Top Medications reports.
*   **Enhanced Top Medications Report:**

Fix flex-aspect-ratio-img-column-012
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=297299
rdar://158173811

Reviewed by Alan Baradlay.

When computing the base size of a flex item, we need to make sure to
ignore any min/max main sizes to match the spec. When a replaced element
is a flex item, we currently handle this case correctly in the flex
item's inline direction but not the block direction. We can fix this by
doing the exact same thing that computeReplacedLogicalWidthRespectinMinMaxWidth
is doing by using a helper function, shouldIgnoreLogicalMinMaxHeightSizes,

author: copilot
body:
This PR fixes Maya scene construction history issues by removing problematic `polyExtrudeFace` nodes and their associated connections from the `aaa.ma` file.

## Problem
The Maya scene file contained three `polyExtrudeFace` nodes (`polyExtrudeFace1`, `polyExtrudeFace2`, `polyExtrudeFace3`) that were creating construction history connection issues. These nodes were chained together in a complex dependency graph that was causing problems when loading or modifying the scene.

## Solution
- **Removed 3 `createNode polyExtrudeFace` statements** and their associated `setAttr` configuration lines
- **Removed 6 `connectAttr` statements** that were connecting the polyExtrudeFace nodes in a chain
- **Added 1 direct connection** from `polyCylinder1.out` to `pCylinderShape1.i` to maintain the geometry pipeline

## Before
```maya
polyCylinder1.out → polyExtrudeFace1.ip
polyExtrudeFace1.out → polyExtrudeFace2.ip  
polyExtrudeFace2.out → polyExtrudeFace3.ip
polyExtrudeFace3.out → pCylinderShape1.i
```

## After
```maya
polyCylinder1.out → pCylinderShape1.i
```

This change eliminates the complex extrusion history while preserving the base cylinder geometry. The Maya scene will now load without the construction history connection errors and should be more stable for further editing.

## Validation
- ✅ No remaining `polyExtrudeFace` references in the file
- ✅ Direct geometry pipeline connection established
- ✅ Maya ASCII file syntax validated
- ✅ File structure integrity maintained

author: javabrett
body:
I exercised this demo and found the following changes I needed to make:

- CP version upgrade to 8.0.0
- Locked Jackson version.  Without this I got a bunch of classloader related problems from floating/different-version dependencies with conflicts from several things that depend on Jackson.
- Changes the DLQ topic name.  This hasn't been done perfectly because I have to repeat myself as I didn't template the value in `pom.xml` where the DQ Rule is defined.  Also the demo failed for me if the DLQ topic was not pre-created - perhaps other Kafka clusters had auto-create on ... but the `orders` topic is explicitly created in the code so I copied this for DLQ topic.
- Code as I found it did not trigger any failures, so no DLQ production.  I changed the random record code so that the producer would sometimes generate records with negative `totalPriceCents` to cause a rule-failure and DLQ.
- Once DLQ records are produced, the first one was killing the producer due to not catching the expection thrown by the DLQ rule handler.  So I reworked the producer exception handling so it can continue, which is what you might expect when DLQing bad records.

body:
# Uv Workspace Migration

This PR contains refactoring of the MATRIX monorepo, migrating from traditional pip-based dependency management (requirements.txt) to uv workspace structure. I also pulled out a set of libraries into standalone folders for usage across other projects 

## 🏗️ uv Workspace Setup

**Complete migration to uv workspace architecture:**
- **Root workspace configuration**: New `pyproject.toml` at repository root defining workspace structure
- **Eliminated requirements.txt files**: Replaced with `pyproject.toml` dependencies across all packages
- **Package modularity**: Each major component now has its own `pyproject.toml` for proper dependency isolation
- **Shared dependency management**: Common dependencies managed at workspace level with automatic linking

## 📚 Library Carve-outs

**Extracted shared functionality into dedicated libraries:**
- **matrix-auth**: Authentication and environment utilities
- **matrix-fabricator**: Data fabrication and generation tools  
- **matrix-gcp-datasets**: GCP integration and Spark utilities
- **matrix-mlflow-utils**: MLflow integration and metric utilities

- had to pull out the Spark hacks we have into a SparkManager so I can extract it into a library and then call from our hooks.py
- Docker build approach, requiring the full repo as build context
- added `kedro experiment retry` functionality

The rest is just renaming stuff


## Notice for contributors

Hi all. We just merged a refactoring of how the matrix monorepo works. We now have several distinct python libraries in `libs/` instead of having it all part of the matrix pipelines project. This requires a few actions from your end:

- delete your .venv in `pipelines/matrix/`
- run `make install` again in `pipelines/matrix`

The new location for the virtual environment is now at the root of the repository which has two benefits:
1. It will be automatically detected by your IDE (tested for VSCode & derivatives) which improves e.g. "go to source" features and autocompletion features
2. avoids having several .venvs for docs/libraries/pipeline etc. One venv is shared across the monorepo

If you see any issues, please respond here and we will help you out.

<!--
 ### Free SaaS Offering Submission

 Thank you for contributing to this list. This list is for **SaaS**
 services that offer a **free tier** to help developers evaluate and
 build something that users can later use and get support for.

 The focus of this list is quite broad but we try to keep things
 limited to that which infrastructure developers, like DevOps Practitioners,
 would find useful.

 This list is the result of more than a thousand people contributing
 to make something useful, we appreciate your efforts.

 ### Code of Conduct

 We are not here to argue with you. If you are argumentative, abusive,
 lie or missrepresent your service or are otherwise anti-social we will
 block you.

 ### Services we do not accept

   * cPanel like PHP + MySQL hosting services.
   * Free dns services that are generic frontends to CloudFlare or similar
   * Services that are verbatim copy pastes of others while adding no value
   * Fake / Temporary / Ephemeral email generators, we have enough of those
-->

 * [x] [Pricing information](https://docs.sms-gate.app/pricing/) is clearly visible without signup or phone calls
